prerequisites: An available chat app in your browser.
A place to keep your final output and review notes.
notice: Use fictional data. Copying a prompt here does not send it to an AI service.
title: Turn customer comments into a service summary
summary: Six comments, a checked table and a useful manager brief.
outcome: A six-row classification table, correct counts and a short evidence-based summary.
body: You work for the fictional service business Cedar Desk. A manager wants to understand recurring issues in six comments. This small sample does not establish what every customer thinks or why a problem happened.

samples.name: Cedar Desk comments
samples.content:
C1: I had to ask twice before someone replied to my first enquiry.
C2: The reply arrived after I had already found another provider.
C3: My request was accepted, but nobody explained what would happen next.
C4: I kept asking for an update because I did not know the status of my request.
C5: The team explained everything clearly and resolved my issue.
C6: I could not understand the labels on the final invoice.

beginner.task: Use the six Cedar Desk comments and the complete classification prompt.
beginner.help: Keep all prompts and the worked answer visible. Pause at every check.
beginner.proof: Save the supplied input, final output and a correction note.

intermediate.task: Create a second fictional input for the same task. Write your prompt before revealing the example.
intermediate.help: Use the checkpoints. Open a prompt or worked answer only when you need a hint.
intermediate.proof: Show how your new input changed the output and apply the same checks.

advanced.task: Solve the same problem family for a different audience with ten fictional records and a written evaluation rubric.
advanced.help: Start from the outcome and rubric. The complete guide is available if a specific step blocks you.
advanced.proof: Save an independent result, a normal test, an incomplete-input test and a misleading-input test.

steps.title: Open a clean conversation
actions: Open your selected chat app in another browser tab: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok or DeepSeek. Use the official tool guide in Learn if you need the starting link.
Choose New chat or the new-conversation control. Keep this workbook open beside it.
Use only the supplied fictional material. Do not upload work or personal information.
steps.expected: You have an empty message box, with no unrelated conversation influencing the task.

steps.title: Read the comments before asking AI
actions: Read all six comments. Group C1–C2 and C3–C4 yourself.
Notice that C6 concerns invoice wording, not an incorrect total.
steps.expected: You have an independent check for the model’s categories.

steps.title: Ask for one category per comment
actions: Paste the complete prompt below into the message box.
Send it and wait for the response.
steps.expected: A table with six rows and the three requested columns.
steps.prompt:
Use only these six fictional Cedar Desk comments. Assign exactly one primary category per comment: Slow initial response; Unclear progress updates; Positive experience; Unclear invoice wording.
Return Comment ID, Primary category and a short supporting quote. Include every ID once. Do not infer causes or claim this sample represents all customers.

C1: I had to ask twice before someone replied to my first enquiry.
C2: The reply arrived after I had already found another provider.
C3: My request was accepted, but nobody explained what would happen next.
C4: I kept asking for an update because I did not know the status of my request.
C5: The team explained everything clearly and resolved my issue.
C6: I could not understand the labels on the final invoice.

steps.title: Compare with the worked answer
actions: Check every ID and quote against the original comment.
If a row differs, ask for a correction using its exact text. Keep the correct rows unchanged.
steps.expected: C1–C2 concern initial response; C3–C4 progress; C5 is positive; C6 concerns wording.

steps.title: Check the counts
actions: Add the counts yourself before moving on.
steps.prompt: Using the checked table, show each category, contributing comment IDs and count. Do not count an ID twice or calculate percentages. Show the total.
steps.ifStuck: If counts differ, compare the contributing IDs rather than asking for a more confident answer.

steps.title: Write a manager brief
actions: Compare the answer with the example; other suggestions can be reasonable if clearly labelled.
steps.expected: Evidence and suggestions appear separately, with no invented cause.
steps.prompt: Write a manager summary under 100 words using only the checked comments and counts. Use two parts: What this sample shows; Suggested actions to test. Refer to IDs, mention this six-comment sample and propose two actions. Do not claim a cause, trend or guaranteed improvement.
steps.example:
In this six-comment sample, two comments describe slow initial replies (C1–C2), two describe unclear updates (C3–C4), one reports a positive resolution (C5), and one describes confusing invoice labels (C6). Causes and wider prevalence remain unknown.
Suggested actions to test: review enquiry acknowledgement; test a clear next-step and status message.

steps.title: Challenge an unsupported conclusion
actions: Check that possible explanations are not presented as facts.
steps.expected: The answer says understaffing is not established.
steps.prompt: Can these comments establish that the team is understaffed? Separate what is known, what is only a possible explanation and what extra evidence we would need.

steps.title: Keep the result and the evidence
actions: Copy your final output into the evidence box at the end of this workbook.
Add what you checked, one weakness you repaired and any remaining limitation.
Select each completion check only after you have performed it. Save your work.
steps.expected: You can explain why your output is usable, not just show that the model produced it.

checks: Suggestions and observed facts are separate.
I tested the unsupported staffing conclusion.
